hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 8(3x + 2)^{-2}$ using the reverse chain rule to get $-\frac{8}{3(3x + 2)} + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative function using the reverse linear chain rule:
$$y = \int 8(3x + 2)^{-2} dx = \frac{8(3x + 2)^{-1}}{-1 \times 3} + c = -\frac{8}{3(3x + 2)} + c$$

Substitute the coordinates of the known point $\left(2, \frac{17}{3}\right)$ into the curve equation:
$$\frac{17}{3} = -\frac{8}{3(3(2) + 2)} + c = -\frac{8}{3(8)} + c = -\frac{1}{3} + c$$
$$c = \frac{17}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{18}{3} = 6$$

State the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = -\frac{8}{3(3x + 2)} + 6$$
